title: Myosin-Driven Textures: Burgers, Sausage, and Lion's Head Meatballs
summary: This ATK Technique video explains how myosin development in ground meat governs texture across burgers, bulk sausage, and meatballs. It contrasts store-bought, highly processed grind with home-style grinding and mixing, showing deliberate controls to limit or maximize myosin release. The host demonstrates burger prep with four small-grind batches, minimal handling, and a brief pre-freeze to set texture, then sears and oven-finishes to a precise internal temperature. The sausage segment covers brining with salt, baking-soda–assisted myosin development, and a stand mixer approach for thorough mixing. The lion’s head meatballs illustrate maximal myosin development, including salt, baking soda, water, and a mixer-assisted blend, followed by long simmering in broth to exploit myosin’s emulsifying role. Throughout, the program reinforces that myosin can both bind water and fat for tenderness and act as a binding agent that can cause toughness if overdeveloped, guiding practical techniques for tender, juicy results in different ground-meat applications.

sections.title: Introduction to myosin and ground-meat texture
concepts: Velcro-like binding of myosin to water, fat, and proteins
sections.description: Opening explanation of myosin as a protein that, when freed from muscle fibers during grinding, can cause toughness if overdeveloped. The host outlines the goal: control myosin development to maintain tenderness across ground-meat preparations.

sections.title: Burger prep run-through: four batches and gentle handling
concepts: four-batch grinding with ~35 pulses per batch
sections.description: The burger workflow is demonstrated: sirloin cut into pieces, spread and frozen briefly, then ground in four batches with precise pulsing. The aim is to keep myosin development minimal to maximize tenderness.

sections.title: Seasoning, handling, and cooking plan for burgers
concepts: salt as main seasoning with light surface pepper
high-heat skillet sear followed by oven finish
sections.description: Patty formation emphasizes minimal handling to avoid excessive myosin development. Salt is used to season and begin binding, followed by two-minute per-side searing and a 300°F oven finish to reach about 125°F internal temperature.

sections.title: Transition to sausage: from salt to myosin-building process
concepts: resting time in fridge (8 hours to 2 days)
fat and water management during grinding
sections.description: The video pivots to bulk sausage, describing salt-driven myosin development, optional use of baking soda, and chilling strategies. The pork is ground with attention to keeping fat cold and to facilitate myosin development through thorough mixing.

sections.title: Lion's head meatballs: maximal myosin development and tenderness
concepts: salt, baking soda, water in the mix
stand mixer as a more effective mixer
sections.description: An example of maximal myosin development is shown via lion's head meatballs. Ground pork is seasoned with salt, baking soda, water, soy, Shaoxing wine, ginger, scallions, and egg, then mixed with a stand mixer. The mixture is formed into meatballs, simmered in broth for an hour and finished to tenderness, illustrating myosin's dual role as binder and emulsifier that retains moisture and fat during long cooking.
